svg.title: The delivery run, from above
svg.desc: An animation, seen from above, of the Lesson 4-9 delivery run on a 4 by 4 grid. The robot starts at home, (0, 0), facing North. The four destinations are numbered 1 to 4: (2, 0), (2, 3), (0, 3) and back to (0, 0). For each leg the planned Manhattan path appears as a dotted line from where the robot is, then the robot drives it: before each step it turns clockwise, one sensor-ended right turn at a time, until it faces the next intersection, then tracks to it and drives past. Leg 1 is one right turn and two steps east. Leg 2 needs three right turns to face North, then three steps up. Leg 3, three right turns to face West, two steps left. Leg 4, three right turns to face South, three steps down to home. Beside it, the main loop with the running line highlighted and a box naming the leg, the step and the heading.
svg.text: drive it; keep where it ends
Each leg is planned from wherever the last
one ended. turn_to() only turns clockwise,
so facing East and wanting North takes
three right turns. That is expected.
